parts.problemMd:
**Discuss **the trade-offs between **image quality** and** file size** when choosing a bitmap image's resolution and colour depth.

Provide **examples **to illustrate your answer.
parts.solutionMd:
**Resolution**

Higher-resolution images have more pixels, which means they contain more detail and have higher quality. However, this also means they have larger file sizes, taking up more storage space and possibly causing slower loading times on websites. On the other hand, lower-resolution images have fewer pixels, which reduces the file size and makes them load faster, but this comes at the cost of image quality, potentially making them look blurry or pixelated when viewed up close or on larger screens.

**Colour depth**

Higher colour depth allows an image to display more colours, leading to better image quality. However, this increases the file size because more bits are needed for each pixel. Lower colour depth reduces the number of colours available, which can make images appear less vibrant but helps in reducing the file size. This is beneficial for faster loading times and less storage usage.

**Examples**

A professional photograph used for printing requires high resolution and high colour depth to ensure excellent quality, but it results in a large file size. In contrast, a thumbnail image on a website typically has low resolution and low colour depth to ensure faster loading times while sacrificing some quality.

> - Demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding with accurate and detailed material **[1 mark]**
> - Applies knowledge directly and consistently with explicit evidence/examples **[1 mark]**
> - Weighs up both sides of the discussion with suitable examples **[1 mark]**

> This is a "Discuss" question worth 8 marks. Marks are awarded using a levels-based approach across three assessment strands:

> - Knowledge and understanding (up to 3 marks): accurate, detailed material covering both resolution and colour depth
> - Application (up to 3 marks): explicit use of examples to support points made
> - Analysis/evaluation (up to 2 marks): weighing up both sides (benefits and drawbacks) of higher/lower resolution and colour depth
> 
> To achieve full marks, candidates must address resolution, colour depth and provide relevant examples. Each property must be discussed in terms of both benefits and drawbacks relating to image quality and file size.
> 
> **[8 marks]**

> 
> For each property (resolution and colour depth), always consider both sides: what happens when it is high and what happens when it is low. A common mistake is to only discuss one direction (e.g. only talking about high resolution) without mentioning the trade-off.
> 
> Your examples should be specific and realistic. Rather than saying "a big image has a big file size", explain the context, e.g. "a professional photograph for printing" versus "a thumbnail on a website". This demonstrates application of knowledge and will help you access the higher mark bands.
> 
> Avoid vague statements such as "it makes it better" — always specify what improves (e.g. image quality, detail, colour accuracy) and what worsens (e.g. file size, loading time, storage requirements).

parts.problemMd:
A compiler and an interpreter are two different types of **translator**.

One similarity between a compiler and an interpreter is that they both translate high‑level language into machine code.

**Explain two **differences between a compiler and an interpreter.
parts.solutionMd:
Two differences between a compiler and an interpreter are:

Any **four **from the following (**MAX 2 **per translator):

- An interpreter translates the code line by line (and executes each line immediately) **[1 mark]**
- … whereas a compiler translates the whole code at the same time (before executing it) **[1 mark]**
- A compiler produces an executable file **[1 mark]**
- … but an interpreter does not **[1 mark]**
- An interpreter is required to run the code each time if used **[1 mark]**
- … whereas a compiler is not **[1 mark]**
- An interpreter stops and reports an error as it is encountered **[1 mark]**
- … whereas a compiler creates a report of all errors at the end of translation **[1 mark]**
- An interpreter will run code up to the point it finds an error **[1 mark]**
- … whereas a compiler will not run the code at all if an error is found **[1 mark]**

parts.problemMd:
Layla uses her computer to create educational games

Layla makes use of **system software**.

One type of system software is the operating system.

**Identify **and **describe two functions** of an operating system.
parts.solutionMd:
Examples of functions of the operating system include:

Any **two** of the following (1 mark for function name, max 2 marks per description):

**User interface ****[1 mark]**

- allows the user to communicate with the hardware **[1 mark]**
- e.g. graphical user interface (GUI) /command prompt **[1 mark]**
- allows the user to input data **[1 mark]**
- outputs data to the user **[1 mark]**

**Memory management/multitasking ****[1 mark]**

- moves data between RAM and VM / manages/allocates RAM between different programs **[1 mark]**
- gets data from RAM / prevents two programs accessing the same memory location **[1 mark]**
- stores data to RAM / enables multitasking **[1 mark]**

**Peripheral management/device drivers ****[1 mark]**

- allows the installation of drivers to communicate with the peripherals **[1 mark]**
- sends data to/from peripherals **[1 mark]**

**User management ****[1 mark]**

- allows the setting up of accounts **[1 mark]**
- security/setting of password **[1 mark]**
- set different access rights **[1 mark]**

**File management ****[1 mark]**

- creation/editing/renaming of files **[1 mark]**
- creation/editing/renaming of folders **[1 mark]**
- movement of files/folders **[1 mark]**

**Handling interrupts ****[1 mark]**

- responding to an event that requires immediate CPU attention **[1 mark]**
- ensuring smooth system operation by processing interrupts **[1 mark]**

**Platform for running applications ****[1 mark]**

- allows application software access to system resources **[1 mark]**

**Providing system security ****[1 mark]**

- offer features like password protection, firewalls, virus scanning, and file encryption** [1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> A sample six mark response could be:
> 
> *The user interface is one function of the operating system. A user interface provides the user with a graphical interface which allows them to interact with the computing, inputting and outputting data.*
> 
> *A second function of an operating system is memory management. Memory management allows data to move between the RAM and virtual memory when RAM becomes full. It also allocates space in RAM for currently in-use programs.*
> 
> - For a 'describe' question, vague statements score no marks — give specific technical detail rather than just restating the function name.
> - Use the exact function labels (e.g. peripheral management, providing system security), not loose terms like 'hardware' or 'security'.

parts.problemMd:
**Explain the role** of **peripheral management** in the operating system.

Include **how **it facilitates **plug-and-play** (**PnP**) functionality
parts.solutionMd:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Role of peripheral management:
> 
> Any 3 from:
> 
> - Handles the way hardware peripherals interact with the software
> - … ensuring that each peripheral operates efficiently
> - … by allocating the necessary system resources
> - Managing data transfer between the computer and the peripheral device
> - Coordinating the operation of multiple peripherals simultaneously
> 
> **[3 marks]**
> 
> PnP functionality:
> 
> - Allows the operating system to automatically detect and configure new peripherals when they are connected
> 
> OR
> 
> - Users do not need to manually install device drivers or restart the system for the peripherals to work
> 
> OR
> 
> - … simplifying the setup and use of hardware **[1 mark]**
> 
> Maximum 3 marks if no mention of PnP functionality
> 
> "Explain" requires candidates to provide a reason or justification for the role of peripheral management, not just a simple statement

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you address both parts of the question: the general role of peripheral management and how it facilitates plug-and-play. Many students focus only on the general role and forget to mention PnP, which limits them to a maximum of 3 marks. A good approach is to write a few points about what peripheral management does (e.g. resource allocation, coordinating devices) and then dedicate at least one clear point to how PnP works, such as automatic detection and configuration of new hardware without needing to manually install drivers.

- Accept a correct expression without the "P =" label (e.g. "(A AND B) OR NOT C") for full marks.
- Accept symbol notation (^ for AND, V for OR, \u00acC or NOT C) interchangeably.

**Write **the **Boolean expression **represented by the logic diagram below:

![Logic circuit diagram featuring an AND gate with inputs A and B, an OR gate outputting P, and a NOT gate with input C. Lines connect gates to the OR gate.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/0fe5f77210f74aaeb3f6c491dfe0263d12db738c/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-computer-science-23/10-boolean-logic/boolean-logic/assets/003-logic-circuit-diagram-featuring-an-and-gate-with.png)
parts.solutionMd:
The Boolean expression for the logic diagram can be expressed as:

- `P = (A AND B) OR (NOT C)` **OR  **`P = (A ^ B) V (¬C)`
- `(A AND B)` **[1 mark]**
- `(NOT C)` **[1 mark]**
- `(A AND B) OR (NOT C)` **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Use parentheses to group each gate's output so the operator precedence is unambiguous
> 
> Match each gate exactly — an OR gate is an inclusive OR, not XOR
